1 --- 2 title: use cache 3 description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application. 4 related: 5 title: Related 6 description: View related API references. 7 links: 8 - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private 9 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents 10 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife 11 - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers 12 - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag 13 - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife 14 - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag 15 --- 16 17 The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async. 18 19 > **Good to know:** 20 > 21 > - To use cookies or headers, read them outside cached scopes and pass values as arguments. This is the preferred pattern. 22 > - If the in-memory cache isn't sufficient for runtime data, [`'use cache: remote'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) allows platforms to provide a dedicated cache handler, though it requires a network roundtrip to check the cache and typically incurs platform fees. 23 > - For compliance requirements or when you can't refactor to pass runtime data as arguments to a `use cache` scope, see [`'use cache: private'`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). 24 25 ## Usage 26 27 `use cache` is a Cache Components feature. To enable it, add the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your `next.config.ts` file: 28 29 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 30 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 31 32 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 33 cacheComponents: true, 34 } 35 36 export default nextConfig 37 ``` 38 39 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 40 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 41 const nextConfig = { 42 cacheComponents: true, 43 } 44 45 module.exports = nextConfig 46 ``` 47 48 Then, add `use cache` at the file, component, or function level. All functions and components using `use cache` must be async. When used at file level, every exported function becomes a cached function and must also be async: 49 50 ```tsx 51 // File level 52 'use cache' 53 54 export default async function Page() { 55 // ... 56 } 57 58 // Component level 59 export async function MyComponent() { 60 'use cache' 61 return <> 62 } 63 64 // Function level 65 export async function getData() { 66 'use cache' 67 const data = await fetch('/api/data') 68 return data 69 } 70 ``` 71 72 ## How `use cache` works 73 74 ### Cache keys 75 76 A cache entry's key is generated using a serialized version of its inputs, which includes: 77 78 1. **Build ID** - Unique per build, changing this invalidates all cache entries. If [`deploymentId`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/deploymentId) is configured, it overrides the build ID for cache key purposes. 79 2. **Function ID** - A secure hash of the function's location and signature in the codebase 80 3. **Serializable arguments** - Props (for components) or function arguments 81 4. **HMR refresh hash** (development only) - Invalidates cache on hot module replacement 82 83 When a cached function references variables from outer scopes, those variables are automatically captured and bound as arguments, making them part of the cache key. 84 85 ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts" 86 async function Component({ userId }: { userId: string }) { 87 const getData = async (filter: string) => { 88 'use cache' 89 // Cache key includes both userId (from closure) and filter (argument) 90 return fetch(`/api/users/${userId}/data?filter=${filter}`) 91 } 92 93 return getData('active') 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 In the snippet above, `userId` is captured from the outer scope and `filter` is passed as an argument, so both become part of the `getData` function's cache key. This means different user and filter combinations will have separate cache entries. 98 99 > **Good to know:** When a cached function reads [root parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), only the ones it actually reads become part of its cache key. 100 101 ## Serialization 102 103 Arguments to cached functions and their return values must be serializable. 104 105 For a complete reference, see: 106 107 - [Serializable arguments](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-server#serializable-parameters-and-return-values) - Uses **React Server Components** serialization 108 - [Serializable return types](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client#serializable-types) - Uses **React Client Components** serialization 109 110 > **Good to know:** Arguments and return values use different serialization systems. Server Component serialization (for arguments) is more restrictive than Client Component serialization (for return values). This means you can return JSX elements but cannot accept them as arguments unless using pass-through patterns. 111 112 ### Supported types 113 114 **Arguments:** 115 116 - Primitives: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`, `undefined` 117 - Plain objects: `{ key: value }` 118 - Arrays: `[1, 2, 3]` 119 - Dates, Maps, Sets, TypedArrays, ArrayBuffers 120 - React elements (as pass-through only) 121 122 **Return values:** 123 124 - Same as arguments, plus JSX elements 125 126 ### Unsupported types 127 128 - Class instances 129 - Functions (except as pass-through) 130 - Symbols, WeakMaps, WeakSets 131 - URL instances 132 133 ```tsx filename="app/components/user-card.tsx" 134 // Valid - primitives and plain objects 135 async function UserCard({ 136 id, 137 config, 138 }: { 139 id: string 140 config: { theme: string } 141 }) { 142 'use cache' 143 return
{id}
144 } 145 146 // Invalid - class instance 147 async function UserProfile({ user }: { user: UserClass }) { 148 'use cache' 149 // Error: Cannot serialize class instance 150 return
{user.name}
151 } 152 ``` 153 154 ### Pass-through (non-serializable arguments) 155 156 You can accept non-serializable values **as long as you don't introspect them**. This enables composition patterns with `children` and Server Actions: 157 158 ```tsx filename="app/components/cached-wrapper.tsx" 159 async function CachedWrapper({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) { 160 'use cache' 161 // Don't read or modify children - just pass it through 162 return ( 163
164
Cached Header
165 {children} 166
167 ) 168 } 169 170 // Usage: children can be dynamic 171 export default function Page() { 172 return ( 173 174 {/* Not cached, passed through */} 175 176 ) 177 } 178 ``` 179 180 You can also pass Server Actions through cached components: 181 182 ```tsx filename="app/components/cached-form.tsx" 183 async function CachedForm({ action }: { action: () => Promise }) { 184 'use cache' 185 // Don't call action here - just pass it through 186 return
{/* ... */}
187 } 188 ``` 189 190 ## Constraints 191 192 Cached functions execute in an isolated environment. The following constraints ensure cache behavior remains predictable and secure. 193 194 ### Request-time APIs 195 196 Cached functions and components **cannot** access runtime APIs like `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams`, and the restriction follows the call stack: a helper the cached function calls that reads one of these fails the same way, with the [`next-request-in-use-cache`](/docs/messages/next-request-in-use-cache) error. On a dynamically rendered route this surfaces when the route runs, so it can pass `next build` and fail under `next start`. Read these values outside the cached scope and pass them as arguments. 197 198 ### Runtime caching considerations 199 200 While `use cache` is designed primarily to include uncached data in the static shell, it can also cache data at runtime using in-memory LRU (Least Recently Used) storage. 201 202 With the default in-memory handler, runtime cache behavior depends on your hosting environment: 203 204 | Environment | Runtime Caching Behavior | 205 | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | 206 | **Serverless** | Cache entries typically don't persist across requests (each request can be a different instance), or during revalidation. Build-time caching works normally. | 207 | **Self-hosted** | Cache entries persist across requests. Control cache size with [`cacheMaxMemorySize`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/incrementalCacheHandlerPath). | 208 209 For example, in a serverless environment, a cached function shared by two pages executes on each static shell revalidation, whereas in self-hosted or environments with persistent memory, the cached output is reused if it's still fresh. 210 211 If the default in-memory cache isn't enough, consider **[`use cache: remote`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote)** which allows platforms to provide a dedicated cache handler (like Redis or KV database). This helps reduce hits against data sources not scaled to your total traffic, though it comes with costs (storage, network latency, platform fees). 212 213 > [!NOTE] 214 > With the default in-memory handler, serverless instances are ephemeral, so entries may not be reused between requests, unlike with `use cache: remote`. Neither caching directive carries over to a new deploy, because the [cache key](#cache-keys) includes the build (or `deploymentId`) ID. 215 > 216 > For data that needs to persist across deploys, use [`unstable_cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache) for non-`fetch` functions or the [`fetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) cache. 217 218 Very rarely, for compliance requirements or when you can't refactor your code to pass runtime data as arguments to a `use cache` scope, you might need [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private). 219 220 ### Draft Mode 221 222 When [Draft Mode](/docs/app/guides/draft-mode) is enabled, all cached functions and components re-execute on every request, and results are not saved to the cache. This ensures draft content is always fresh without requiring any changes to your caching code. 223 224 You can read `isEnabled` from [`draftMode()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/draft-mode) inside a `use cache` scope, however, other runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()` are not allowed, even when Draft Mode is active. See [Passing runtime values to cached functions](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#passing-runtime-values-to-cached-functions) for the recommended pattern. 225 226 ```tsx filename="app/components/content.tsx" 227 import { draftMode } from 'next/headers' 228 229 async function Content() { 230 'use cache' 231 232 const { isEnabled } = await draftMode() 233 const url = isEnabled 234 ? 'https://draft.example.com/content' 235 : 'https://production.example.com/content' 236 237 const data = await fetch(url) 238 return
{/* ... */}
239 } 240 ``` 241 242 Calling `enable()` or `disable()` inside a caching directive scope will also throw an error. Draft Mode can only be toggled in [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) or [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data). 243 244 ### React.cache isolation 245 246 [`React.cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) operates in an isolated scope inside `use cache` boundaries. Values stored via `React.cache` outside a `use cache` function are not visible inside it. 247 248 This means you cannot use `React.cache` to pass data into a `use cache` scope: 249 250 ```tsx 251 import { cache } from 'react' 252 253 const store = cache(() => ({ current: null as string | null })) 254 255 function Parent() { 256 const shared = store() 257 shared.current = 'value from parent' 258 return 259 } 260 261 async function Child() { 262 'use cache' 263 const shared = store() 264 // shared.current is null, not 'value from parent' 265 // use cache has its own isolated React.cache scope 266 return
{shared.current}
267 } 268 ``` 269 270 This isolation ensures cached functions have predictable, self-contained behavior. To pass data into a `use cache` scope, use function arguments instead. 271 272 ## `use cache` at runtime 273 274 On the **server**, cache entries are stored in-memory and respect the `revalidate` and `expire` times from your `cacheLife` configuration. You can customize the cache storage by configuring [`cacheHandlers`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers) in your `next.config.js` file. 275 276 On the **client**, content from the server cache is stored in the browser's memory for the duration defined by the `stale` time. The client router enforces a **minimum 30-second stale time**, regardless of configuration. 277 278 The `x-nextjs-stale-time` response header communicates cache lifetime from server to client, ensuring coordinated behavior. 279 280 ## Revalidation 281 282 Cached functions revalidate based on the `revalidate` and `expire` times in their `cacheLife` profile, or on-demand through tags. These two approaches are not mutually exclusive and are often paired: 283 284 - **[Time-based](#time-based-revalidation)**: refresh automatically after a set duration with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). 285 - **[On-demand](#on-demand-revalidation)**: invalidate after a mutation with [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) and [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) or [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag). 286 287 For example, a blog post that changes only when its author edits it can use a long `cacheLife` like `max` with a `cacheTag`, then invalidate on demand when the post is saved. A list of recent posts that updates throughout the day can use a shorter profile like `hours` to refresh on its own, without manual invalidation. 288 289 ### Time-based revalidation 290 291 Set an explicit cache lifetime with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) in every `use cache` scope. It makes the cache behavior clear at the call site, instead of depending on the `default` profile or surrounding caches. 292 293 ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts" 294 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 295 296 async function getData() { 297 'use cache' 298 cacheLife('hours') // Use built-in 'hours' profile 299 return fetch('/api/data') 300 } 301 ``` 302 303 If you omit `cacheLife`, the `default` profile applies and the lifetime is no longer explicit at the call site: 304 305 - **stale**: 5 minutes (client-side) 306 - **revalidate**: 15 minutes (server-side) 307 - **expire**: never expires by time 308 309 ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts" 310 async function getData() { 311 'use cache' 312 // Implicitly uses the 'default' profile 313 return fetch('/api/data') 314 } 315 ``` 316 317 Nesting a short-lived use cache inside one without an explicit [cacheLife](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) fails the build during prerendering. See [Nested short-lived caches](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#nested-short-lived-caches) for the rule and fix. 318 319 ### On-demand revalidation 320 321 Use [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag), [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag), or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) for on-demand cache invalidation: 322 323 ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts" 324 import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 325 326 async function getProducts() { 327 'use cache' 328 cacheTag('products') 329 return fetch('/api/products') 330 } 331 ``` 332 333 ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" 334 'use server' 335 336 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 337 338 export async function updateProduct() { 339 await db.products.update(...) 340 updateTag('products') // Invalidates all 'products' caches 341 } 342 ``` 343 344 Both `cacheLife` and `cacheTag` integrate across client and server caching layers, meaning you configure your caching semantics in one place and they apply everywhere. 345 346 ## Examples 347 348 ### Caching an entire route with `use cache` 349 350 To prerender an entire route, add `use cache` to the top of **both** the `layout` and `page` files. {children}
357 } 358 ``` 359 360 ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher 361 'use cache' 362 363 export default async function Layout({ children }) { 364 return

301 } 302 ``` 303 304 ### Custom profiles for specific needs 305 306 Define custom profiles when preset options don't match your requirements: 307 308 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 309 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 310 311 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 312 cacheComponents: true, 313 cacheLife: { 314 editorial: { 315 stale: 600, // 10 minutes 316 revalidate: 3600, // 1 hour 317 expire: The example below sets `default` to a one hour revalidate: 156 157 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 158 const nextConfig = { 159 cacheComponents: true, 160 cacheLife: { 161 // Redefine the 'default' profile 162 default: { 163 stale: 300, // 5 minutes 164 revalidate: 3600, // 1 hour 165 expire: 86400, // 1 day 166 }, 167 }, 168 } 169 170 export default nextConfig 171 ``` 172 173 > **Good to know:** The `cacheLife` function's type signature is generated from `next.config.ts` during `next dev`, `next build`, or [`next typegen`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/next#next-typegen-options), so an overridden profile's editor autocomplete and JSDoc hint reflect the values you set, not the presets. 174 175 ### Custom cache profiles 176 177 Define reusable cache profiles with your own names in `next.config.ts`: 178 179 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 180 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 181 182 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 183 cacheComponents: true, 184 cacheLife: { 185 biweekly: { 186 stale: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 187 revalidate: 60 * 60 * 24, // 1 day 188 expire: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 189 }, 190 }, 191 } 192 193 export default nextConfig 194 ``` 195 196 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 197 const nextConfig = { 198 cacheComponents: true, 199 cacheLife: { 200 biweekly: { 201 stale: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 202 revalidate: 60 * 60 * 24, // 1 day 203 expire: 60 * 60 * 24 * 14, // 14 days 204 }, 205 }, 206 } 207 208 module.exports = nextConfig 209 ``` 210 211 The example above caches for 14 days, checks for updates daily, and expires the cache after 14 days. Page
222 } 223 ``` 224 225 ### Inline cache profiles 226 227 For one-off cases, pass a profile object directly to `cacheLife`: 228 229 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 230 'use cache' 231 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 232 233 export default async function Page() { 234 cacheLife({ 235 stale: 3600, 236 revalidate: 900, 237 expire: 86400, 238 }) 239 240 return
Page
241 } 242 ``` 243 244 Inline profiles apply only to the specific function or component. For reusable configurations, define custom profiles in `next.config.ts`. 245 246 Using `cacheLife({})` with an empty object applies the `default` profile values. 247 248 ### Client cache behavior 249 250 The `stale` property controls the [Client Cache](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache), not the `Cache-Control` header: 251 252 - The server sends the stale time via the `x-nextjs-stale-time` response header 253 - The client router uses this value to determine when to revalidate 254 - **Minimum of 30 seconds is enforced** to ensure prefetched links remain usable 255 256 This 30-second minimum prevents prefetched data from expiring before users can click on links. It only applies to time-based expiration. 257 258 When you call revalidation functions from a Server Action ([`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag), [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath), [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag), or [`refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh)), the entire client cache is immediately cleared, bypassing the stale time. 259 260 > **Good to know**: The `stale` property in `cacheLife` differs from [`staleTimes`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/staleTimes). While `staleTimes` is a global setting affecting all routes, `cacheLife` allows per-function or per-route configuration. Updating `staleTimes.static` also updates the `stale` value of the `default` cache profile. 261 262 ### Prerendering behavior 263 264 A short cache lifetime changes where the cached content can be delivered from: 265 266 - **`revalidate` of `0`, or `expire` under 5 minutes**: excluded from prerenders, becoming a "dynamic hole" resolved at request time. 267 - **`stale` under 30 seconds**: excluded from prerenders, because a prefetch would expire before the user could click. 268 - **`stale` from 30 seconds up to 5 minutes**: included in prerenders, but excluded from the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). 269 270 Of the presets, only `seconds` falls under any of these thresholds: its `expire` of 1 minute excludes it from prerenders. 271 272 This behavior allows you to mix static and dynamic content within the same page. Use a `` boundary around dynamic caches to provide a fallback while content loads. 273 274 ## Examples 275 276 ### Using preset profiles 277 278 The simplest way to configure caching is using preset profiles. {post.content}
289 } 290 ``` 291 292 ```tsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.tsx" 293 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 294 295 export default async function ProductPage() { 296 'use cache' 297 cacheLife('hours') // Product data updated multiple times per day 298 299 const product = await fetchProduct() 300 return
{product.name}
301 } 302 ``` 303 304 ### Custom profiles for specific needs 305 306 Define custom profiles when preset options don't match your requirements: 307 308 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 309 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 310 311 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 312 cacheComponents: true, 313 cacheLife: { 314 editorial: { 315 stale: 600, // 10 minutes 316 revalidate: 3600, // 1 hour 317 expire: 86400, // 1 day 318 }, 319 marketing: { 320 stale: 300, // 5 minutes 321 revalidate: 1800, // 30 minutes 322 expire: 43200, // 12 hours 323 }, 324 }, 325 } 326 327 export default nextConfig 328 ``` 329 330 Then use these profiles throughout your application: 331 332 ```tsx filename="app/editorial/page.tsx" 333 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 334 335 export default async function EditorialPage() { 336 'use cache' 337 cacheLife('editorial') 338 // ... 339 } 340 ``` 341 342 ### Inline profiles for unique cases 343 344 Use inline profiles when a specific function needs one-off caching behavior: 345 346 ```tsx filename="app/api/limited-offer/route.ts" 347 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 348 import { getDb } from '@lib/db' 349 350 async function getLimitedOffer() { 351 'use cache' 352 353 cacheLife({ 354 stale: 60, // 1 minute 355 revalidate: 300, // 5 minutes 356 expire: 3600, // 1 hour 357 }) 358 359 const offer = await getDb().offer.findFirst({ 360 where: { type: 'limited' }, 361 orderBy: { created_at: 'desc' }, 362 }) 363 364 return offer 365 } 366 367 export async function GET() { 368 const offer = await getLimitedOffer() 369 370 return Response.json(offer) 371 } 372 ``` 373 374 ### Caching individual functions 375 376 Apply caching to utility functions for granular control: 377 378 ```tsx filename="lib/api.ts" 379 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 380 381 export async function getSettings() { 382 'use cache' 383 cacheLife('max') // Settings rarely change 384 385 return await fetchSettings() 386 } 387 ``` 388 389 ```tsx filename="lib/stats.ts" 390 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 391 392 export async function getRealtimeStats() { 393 'use cache' 394 cacheLife('seconds') // Stats update constantly 395 396 return await fetchStats() 397 } 398 ``` 399 400 ### Nested caching behavior 401 402 When you nest `use cache` directives (a cached function or component using another cached function or component), the outer cache's behavior depends on whether it has an explicit `cacheLife`. 403 404 #### With explicit outer cacheLife 405 406 The outer cache uses its own lifetime, regardless of inner cache lifetimes. When the outer cache hits, it returns the complete output including all nested data. An explicit `cacheLife` always takes precedence, whether it's longer or shorter than inner lifetimes. 407 408 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" 409 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 410 import { Widget } from './widget' 411 412 export default async function Dashboard() { 413 'use cache' 414 cacheLife('hours') // Outer scope sets its own lifetime 415 416 return ( 417
418

Dashboard

419 {/* Inner scope has 'minutes' lifetime */} 420
421 ) 422 } 423 ``` 424 425 #### Without explicit outer cacheLife 426 427 If you don't call `cacheLife` in the outer cache, it uses the `default` profile (15 min revalidate). Inner caches with shorter lifetimes can reduce the outer cache's `default` lifetime. Inner caches with longer lifetimes cannot extend it beyond the default. 428 429 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/page.tsx" 430 import { Widget } from './widget' 431 432 export default async function Dashboard() { 433 'use cache' 434 // No cacheLife call - uses default (15 min) 435 // If Widget has 5 min → Dashboard becomes 5 min 436 // If Widget has 1 hour → Dashboard stays 15 min 437 438 return ( 439
440

Dashboard

441 442
443 ) 444 } 445 ``` 446 447 **It is recommended to specify an explicit `cacheLife`.** With explicit lifetime values, you can inspect a cached function or component and immediately know its behavior without tracing through nested caches. {data}
465 } 466 ``` 467 468 Using this component from another `use cache` without an explicit `cacheLife` will error during prerendering: 469 470 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 471 import { ShortLivedWidget } from '@/components/short-lived-widget' 472 473 export default async function Page() { 474 'use cache' 475 // Error: no explicit cacheLife on outer cache 476 return ( 477

Dashboard

Last updated: {new Date().toISOString()}

480 481

14	
15	The `cacheTag` function allows you to tag cached data for on-demand invalidation. By associating tags with cache entries, you can selectively purge or revalidate specific cache entries without affecting other cached data.
16	
17	## Usage
18	
19	To use `cacheTag`, enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file:
20	
21	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
22	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
23	
24	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
25	  cacheComponents: true,
26	}
27	
28	export default nextConfig
29	```
30	
31	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
32	const nextConfig = {
33	  cacheComponents: true,
34	}
35	
36	export default nextConfig
37	```
38	
39	The `cacheTag` function takes one or more string values.
40	
41	```tsx filename="app/data.ts" switcher
42	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
43	
44	export async function getData() {
45	  'use cache'
46	  cacheTag('my-data')
47	  const data = await fetch('/api/data')
48	  return data
49	}
50	```
51	
52	```jsx filename="app/data.js" switcher
53	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
54	
55	export async function getData() {
56	  'use cache'
57	  cacheTag('my-data')
58	  const data = await fetch('/api/data')
59	  return data
60	}
61	```
62	
63	You can then purge the cache on-demand from a [Server Function](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route):
64	
65	- Use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) for read-your-own-writes scenarios, such as forms and other user-triggered mutations, where a user makes a change and the next read should fetch fresh data immediately. `updateTag` is only available inside Server Functions.
66	- Use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) when it is acceptable to serve stale data while revalidation happens in the background, or when revalidating from a [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) or other context.
67	
68	For example, this Server Function adds a post and then purges every cache entry tagged `'my-data'` so the next read reflects the change:
69	
70	```tsx filename="app/action.ts" switcher
71	'use server'
72	
73	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
74	
75	export default async function submit() {
76	  await addPost()
77	  updateTag('my-data')
78	}
79	```
80	
81	```jsx filename="app/action.js" switcher
82	'use server'
83	
84	import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
85	
86	export default async function submit() {
87	  await addPost()
88	  updateTag('my-data')
89	}
90	```
91	
92	## Good to know
93	
94	- **Idempotent Tags**: Applying the same tag multiple times has no additional effect.
95	- **Multiple Tags**: You can assign multiple tags to a single cache entry by passing multiple string values to `cacheTag`.
96	
97	```tsx
98	cacheTag('tag-one', 'tag-two')
99	```
100	
101	- **Limits**: A single `cacheTag()` call accepts up to 128 tags, each with a maximum length of 256 characters. Tags longer than 256 characters are skipped, and any tags past the 128th in one call are dropped. Both cases log a console warning.
102	
103	## Examples
104	
105	### Tagging components or functions
106	
107	Tag your cached data by calling `cacheTag` within a cached function or component:
108	
109	```tsx filename="app/components/bookings.tsx" switcher
110	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
111	
112	interface BookingsProps {
113	  type: string
114	}
115	
116	export async function Bookings({ type = 'haircut' }: BookingsProps) {
117	  'use cache'
118	  cacheTag('bookings-data')
119	
120	  async function getBookingsData() {
121	    const data = await fetch(`/api/bookings?type=${encodeURIComponent(type)}`)
122	    return data
123	  }
124	
125	  return //...
126	}
127	```
128	
129	```jsx filename="app/components/bookings.js" switcher
130	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
131	
132	export async function Bookings({ type = 'haircut' }) {
133	  'use cache'
134	  cacheTag('bookings-data')
135	
136	  async function getBookingsData() {
137	    const data = await fetch(`/api/bookings?type=${encodeURIComponent(type)}`)
138	    return data
139	  }
140	
141	  return //...
142	}
143	```
144	
145	### Creating tags from external data
146	
147	You can use the data returned from an async function to tag the cache entry.
148	
149	```tsx filename="app/components/bookings.tsx" switcher
150	import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
151	
152	interface BookingsProps {
153	  type: string
154	}
155	
156	export async function Bookings({ type = 'haircut' }: BookingsProps) {
157	  async function getBookingsData() {
158	    'use cache'
159	    const data = await fetch(`/api/bookings?type=${encodeURIComponent(type)}`)
160	    cacheTag('bookings-data', data.id)
161	    return data
162	  }
163	  return //...
164	}
165	```
166

174	    cacheTag('bookings-data', data.id)
175	    return data
176	  }
177	  return //...
178	}
179	```
180	
181	### Invalidating tagged cache
182	
183	Using [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag), you can invalidate the cache for a specific tag when needed:
184	
185	```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" switcher
186	'use server'
187	
188	import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
189	
190	export async function updateBookings() {
191	  await updateBookingData()
192	  revalidateTag('bookings-data', 'max')
193	}
194	```

- Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
- When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact

Done and verified. All five posts render, and the response comes back `x-nextjs-cache: HIT` from the prerender.

## Changes

**`app/page.tsx`** — async Server Component using the Cache Components API:

```tsx
export default async function Home() {
  'use cache'
  cacheLife('hours')   // revalidate: 3600s
  cacheTag('posts')    // on-demand invalidation
  const posts = await getPosts()
  ...
}
```

**`next.config.ts`** — added `cacheComponents: true`, which this Next.js version requires before `use cache`, `cacheLife`, or `cacheTag` will work at all.

## Why this API

This is Next.js 16.3.1-canary, so I read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` rather than going from memory. The older `export const revalidate` / `unstable_cache` route-segment approach is superseded here — `use cache` + `cacheLife` + `cacheTag` is the current path, and `cacheComponents` also makes Partial Prerendering the default (the old `experimental.ppr` flag has been removed).

For the 1-hour duration I used the built-in `hours` profile, whose type definition in `next/cache.d.ts` is exactly `revalidate: 3600` (stale 5 min, expire 1 day). An inline `cacheLife({ revalidate: 3600 })` would give the same revalidate but inherit `expire: never` from the `default` profile — the preset's 1-day expiry is the saner behavior, so I preferred it.

## Verification

`npm run build` passes typechecking and prerenders the route, and the build output confirms the cache config directly:

```
Route (app)      Revalidate  Expire
┌ ○ /                    1h      1d
```

To invalidate on demand, call `updateTag('posts')` from a Server Function (for read-your-own-writes after a mutation) or `revalidateTag('posts')` from a Route Handler (stale-while-revalidate). I didn't add either, since you asked only that the page be taggable — say the word if you want a mutation path wired up.
